expectations.text: tfctl was called with the invalid run ID run-NONEXISTENT12345
expectations.evidence: commands.log: '"run_id":"run-NONEXISTENT12345"' from the script's tfctl /runs/{id} call.

expectations.text: The output clearly communicates that the run was not found or an error occurred
expectations.evidence: Response line 1: 'Could not retrieve policy evaluations for run `run-NONEXISTENT12345`.'

expectations.text: The error message includes the specific run ID 'run-NONEXISTENT12345'
expectations.evidence: Run ID appears in response lines 1, 3, and 12.

expectations.text: The response stops at the first failed API call — no follow-up calls to /task-stages or /policy-evaluations are attempted with this invalid ID
expectations.evidence: commands.log contains only the 'run lookup failed' error from the initial /runs/{id} call; no task-stages or policy-evaluations entries.

expectations.text: No fabricated policy evaluations, policy-sets, or outcomes are shown in the response
expectations.evidence: Response contains only the error message and recovery hints — no policy data.

expectations.text: The response surfaces the actual error wording from tfctl/stderr (e.g. 'Resource not found', 'unauthorized') rather than a generic 'an error occurred' message
expectations.evidence: Line 4 quotes verbatim: 'Resource not found or you are unauthorized to this action. Check your account permissions.'

expectations.text: The response offers at least one concrete recovery suggestion (verify the run ID, check active profile, or run tfctl profile display) rather than just reporting failure
expectations.evidence: Lines 6-12 suggest `tfctl profile display`, `tfctl auth info`, and double-checking the run ID.
